- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, reduce forecasted peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), increase forecasted lows to account for downward pressure.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending upward, model often overestimates — apply a 3–5% downward bias.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast to align with recent mean.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon — apply a 2–5% downward correction for days 1–7.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish signals, model tends to lag — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts.
